alignments.note: Interrogative Τί carries content of its own (rule 64) and is aligned to What in the ordinary way.

Verbless clause Τί ὄφελος: the ASV verbalizes the predicate noun, so the supplied doth it rides with ὄφελος and the head is the lexical word profit (rules 62, 68, 17). The dummy subject it and the auxiliary doth are the supplied verb's own, and rule 68 puts both on the noun because the Greek clause expresses no subject for them.
Genitive pronoun rendered by the possessive my; no article stands here to be displaced (rule 20).
Anarthrous vocative and the ASV supplies no address word, so the noun stands alone; no article competes (rule 89).
Ordinary conditional ἐάν → if (rule 72's closing clause).

Anarthrous indefinite; the supplied a is a rule 7 helper on the noun the ASV writes for τις, as rule 62's εἴ τις → any man keeps the whole phrase on the indefinite. Head on man, the nominal word realizing the indefinite; a bare determiner is not a candidate head under rule 17.
Subjunctive rendered by the bare say.

The ASV expands the infinitive into a finite clause; the supplied subject he is a rule 74 helper on the infinitive itself, and rule 9 heads the unit on the lexical verb hath rather than on the pronoun. No complementizer is written, so rule 85 is not in question.
Subjunctive rendered by the bare have.
Ordinary negative μή → not; ἔργα is not a negative indefinite, so rules 41 and 59 do not empty it, and rule 44 does not reach a negator that is not marking the question.

Interrogative μή expecting a negative answer; the ASV marks the question by inversion alone (can that faith save him?) and supplies no interrogative word, so rule 44 leaves it empty. The expressed δύναται keeps can under rule 64's clause that a verb the clause required anyway is not a supplied word — the contrast being μήτι … ἐστιν → Can this be, where Can is supplied over an expressed copula. A reference comparison will report this as a disagreement, and that report is not a correction.
δύναται → can; the modal is the expressed verb's own English, not a word supplied for the interrogative particle.

The ASV renders the article by the supplied demonstrative that; rule 60 aligns it there, no Greek demonstrative competing for the slot. The competing reading would leave it unrepresented under rule 23, but that rule is for an article English realizes nowhere.
Head noun bare, its determiner having gone to the article (rules 57, 60).
Infinitive complement of δύναται; English writes no separate to after the modal.

review_notes: Reviewed against the contract and returned unchanged; every unit's status, edges and head check out. Every s### and t### appears exactly once (19 source, 22 target).

s014 interrogative μή is the one unrepresented unit. Rule 44's test is the English: the ASV marks the question by inversion of the expressed δύναται, supplying no interrogative word, so nothing answers to the particle. Rule 64's μήτι → Can is the contrast, and it does not apply because can here is the expressed verb's own gloss rather than a supplied frame. The reference comparison's disagreement on this token is expected.

s002 ὄφελος carries the supplied doth it under the rule 53/62/68 chain: the clause is verbless, the Greek expresses no subject, and the predicate noun the ASV verbalizes is what is left to carry the supplied words. Head on profit under rule 17, the lexical word realizing ὄφελος; Τί keeps only What.

s016 ἡ is aligned to the supplied demonstrative that under rule 60 rather than left unrepresented. No Greek demonstrative competes for the determiner slot, so rules 38 and 49 are not in play; the alternative rule 23 reading is named in that unit's note.

s008 τις → a man is headed on man, following rule 62's placement of the whole phrase on the indefinite and rule 17's refusal to head a unit on a bare determiner. Rule 69's head on any is not counter-precedent: there any is a quantifier carrying the indefinite sense, whereas a is only the supplied article.

s009 ἔχειν → he hath keeps the supplied subject on the infinitive under rule 74, headed on the lexical verb under rule 9. No complementizer is supplied here, so rule 85 and rule 74's closing aside are not engaged.

Variant SBLGNT.JAS.2.14.v012 is underdetermined with the base among the compatible readings and carries no FALLBACK EXCLUDED mark, so rule 97 does not apply and no textual decision was made here (rule 12).
